about.full:
I'm a Computer Science graduate student at Stevens Institute of Technology (GPA: 3.91) currently interning at Sport Squad, Inc. (JOOLA) as a Business Development Intern — building AI-powered tools using generative, agentic, and embedded AI on the Shopify platform.

I've worked across the full stack: React, Next.js, Flask, Node.js on the frontend and backend; TensorFlow, Scikit-learn, OpenAI GPT for machine learning and AI; and Power BI, DAX, and ETL pipelines for data analytics. I've shipped everything from CNN-based image classifiers to multi-page Streamlit AI applications.

Previously, I was a Graduate Teaching Assistant for CS 555: Agile Methods at Stevens, helping 40+ students with Scrum, Kanban, and sprint planning. Before that, I interned at Tata Consultancy Services building Power BI dashboards and data models for service monitoring.

I don't consider it enough for something to just work. I care about clean architecture, maintainable code, and software that actually solves real problems. My current goal is to keep building at the intersection of AI and full-stack — systems that are both intelligent and intuitive.

projects.intro: A collection of *AI systems*, *full-stack products*, and *data tools* built to solve **real problems**.

items.title: AI Study Buddy
items.tagline: Turns lecture PDFs into summaries, flashcards, quizzes, and a spaced-repetition plan.
items.description: A multi-page AI study assistant that transforms lecture notes and PDFs into summaries, flashcards, quizzes, and interactive Q&A — with spaced repetition planning and difficulty-based flashcard tracking.
highlights: Multi-page study assistant that auto-generates summaries, flashcards, quizzes, and interactive Q&A from uploaded lecture PDFs, cutting study preparation time by 60%.
Structured JSON prompts produce reliable MCQ and true/false questions with explanations, achieving 90% alignment with the source material.
AI-powered spaced-repetition planner with difficulty-based flashcard tracking and session analytics to personalize study schedules.

decisions.title: Structured JSON Prompts
decisions.detail: Forcing a JSON schema on generation makes quiz output parseable and repeatable instead of free-text that breaks the UI.

decisions.title: Streamlit Multi-Page
decisions.detail: Page-per-mode keeps summary, flashcards, quiz, and Q&A state isolated without a separate frontend framework.

items.title: Emoji Detection System
items.tagline: CNN emoji classifier hitting 94% accuracy with sub-200ms real-time inference.
items.description: Deep learning emoji classifier using CNNs with 94% accuracy across 7 categories. Features real-time GUI prediction with sub-200ms inference latency and full data augmentation pipeline.
highlights: Trained a Convolutional Neural Network with data augmentation to classify 7 emoji categories, reaching 94% accuracy on F1-score evaluation.
Streamlined image preprocessing by 60% with batch normalization and optimized OpenCV transforms for resizing, normalization, and augmentation.
Deployed behind an interactive GUI for user-uploaded prediction, delivering real-time inference under 200ms latency.

decisions.title: Batch Normalization
decisions.detail: Stabilizes training on a small, augmented dataset and lets the network converge at a higher learning rate.

decisions.title: Augmentation First
decisions.detail: Rotation, flip, and zoom variants prevent the CNN from memorizing a limited set of emoji renderings.

items.title: ConvLSTM Video Classification
items.tagline: Spatiotemporal video classification served as a production Flask REST API.
items.description: Spatiotemporal video classification pipeline using ConvLSTM architecture for extracting temporal features from video sequences, deployed as a production-ready Flask REST API.
highlights: ConvLSTM architecture captures both spatial and temporal features across video frame sequences rather than classifying frames in isolation.
OpenCV frame-extraction pipeline samples, resizes, and normalizes sequences into fixed-length tensors ready for training.
Packaged as a Flask REST API so the trained model can be called as a service instead of run from a notebook.

decisions.title: ConvLSTM over CNN
decisions.detail: Frame-by-frame CNNs lose motion. ConvLSTM cells keep convolutional structure while carrying state across the sequence.

decisions.title: Flask API Layer
decisions.detail: Wrapping the model in REST endpoints makes it callable from any client instead of locked inside a training notebook.
